content:
For a SaaS business, a service error, unauthorized access and a cloud provider outage are different events. SaaS means software supplied as a service, often by subscription. A company in Moldova should describe the function customers use, the obligations it accepted and the consequences being assessed. A product name does not confirm that every subscription, integration or AI feature is insurable.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. The 2027 scenarios are planning examples, not forecasts or confirmation of individual insurance terms.

Who needs this review?

Founders and managers of subscription platforms, hosted business applications and software services should compare sales promises with signed commitments. Record which entity supplies the service, which providers support it and which countries customers operate in. A standard availability statement on a website is not necessarily the same obligation as a negotiated service-level agreement. Retain the relevant versions.

Separate service failure from cyber loss

A faulty calculation may produce a customer's financial demand without an attack. An attack may require restoration of the company's systems without proving a professional error. A cloud outage can interrupt delivery without damaging owned equipment. Ask separately about professional liability, incident expenses and business interruption. These are assessment categories, not evidence of an available combined policy in Moldova.

Exclusions and promises to examine

Check contractual penalties, service credits, guarantees of results, known defects, intellectual-property allegations and dependence on providers. Establish whether correcting the company's own service is treated differently from a third party's claim. Read applicable dates, notification requirements, territories and jurisdictions. A customer demanding particular wording does not mean an insurer has accepted it or that the broker may certify it.

INTACT publishes a general professional-liability product presentation. INTACT: professional liability presentation. Checked 25 November 2026. It does not confirm SaaS, AI features, international contracts or availability through ING Broker; its broad rate range is not used as a SaaS quotation.

Price and submission quality

Assessment may depend on revenue, functions, customer sectors, countries, contract limits, subcontracting, security controls and loss history. There is no verified general SaaS tariff for 2027. A professional-liability percentage for a different activity cannot be converted into an exact software quotation. Compare responses using identical service descriptions and separate conditional indications from final policy terms.

Plan AI-assisted features for 2027

Treat a new AI function, external model provider or automated customer decision as a planning scenario, not a prediction of regulation or claim frequency. In an illustrative subscription platform, an automated recommendation changes a customer's workflow. Clarify whether it is advisory, who approves use and what evidence of testing is retained. Terms supplied by the model vendor do not automatically transfer every responsibility arising from your own client agreement.

Records that make assessment practical

Prepare architecture at a non-sensitive level, dependencies, service descriptions, anonymized contract extracts, customer countries, release controls and a factual complaint history. Do not provide keys, source code or client records through a public form. Keep change approvals linked to the deployed release. Following an incident, use qualified response and legal support and follow the relevant notification procedure without inventing a cause or promising reimbursement.

A 2026 dependency signal for 2027 service planning

ENISA's 2026 assessment discusses third-party attacks, drawing on 2025 EU events.

This is not a measured trend in Moldova SaaS insurance purchases. Our editorial planning inference is that a platform should map the suppliers behind authentication, hosting and customer notifications before expanding its 2027 service promises. For each dependency, identify the owner of recovery decisions and the evidence that service has resumed. Ask separately about a professional claim from a failed service and the platform's own incident expenses. That distinction may help determine which insurance questions deserve assessment, but supplier dependence does not prove negligence, an accepted claim or availability of any particular SaaS policy.

Practical risk prevention

Keep release approval, testing evidence and rollback responsibilities traceable. Review supplier dependence and test recovery without exposing customer data. Give AI-generated changes the same controlled review as other changes. Align service promises with actual delivery and obtain legal review of exceptional commitments. Operational discipline is useful regardless of whether a suitable insurance solution is ultimately available.

Three service situations with different evidence

These are hypothetical decision situations, not actual client cases or a list of accepted benefits.

  • A calculation in the service produces a client demand: compare the promised function, release, acceptance and alleged consequence. Correcting the platform and addressing a third-party financial demand are not automatically the same expense.
  • A hosting provider becomes unavailable: map dependent functions, recovery rights and the customer's actual interruption. A supplier incident needs separate consideration from a defect in your own professional service.
  • The company grants contractual service credits: retain the relevant commitment and the event calculation. Commercially agreeing a credit does not itself demonstrate accepted professional liability or reimbursable interruption.

Frequently asked questions

Which information affects the price of a SaaS insurance enquiry?

Explain service functions, revenue, customer sectors and countries, contract commitments, dependencies and complaint history. Compare proposals against identical information. A public professional-liability rate for another occupation does not establish a software-service quotation.

What documents make a SaaS submission useful?

Prepare a non-sensitive dependency map, service description, anonymized contract extracts, customer-country information, release controls and factual complaint history. Agree the need for further material. Do not send source code, credentials or customer data through public forms.

What records matter when a service error produces a client demand?

Retain the relevant requirement, release, tests, acceptance and demand with dates. Obtain appropriate technical and legal assistance and follow the applicable notification procedure. Distinguish the client's allegation, verified effect and insurer's contractual assessment.

How should service credits be compared with potential insured loss?

Identify the promise in the client contract and the event causing the credit. Ask separately about contractual credits, correcting the service and third-party claims. Commercially agreeing a credit does not prove that an insurer accepts that expense.

When a SaaS customer alleges a professional service error, compare that question with IT professional liability: contracts, delivery and client claims. This does not establish acceptance of every service credit, software function or AI feature.

How should a new AI feature be included in the risk file?

Explain what it changes for customers, who approves output, how it is tested and which providers it depends on. Request review of the changed service before claiming protection. AI use neither proves professional negligence nor creates an insurance endorsement.
